questions.q: What does innodb_buffer_pool_size control, per this lesson?
options: The size of InnoDB's in-memory cache for table and index data
The maximum number of client connections allowed
The size of the binary log files
The number of CPU cores MySQL can use
questions.explain: innodb_buffer_pool_size is the size of InnoDB's in-memory cache, avoiding disk reads for data already cached.

questions.q: Per this lesson, roughly what portion of RAM does a common real-world guideline suggest for innodb_buffer_pool_size on a dedicated database server?
options: Roughly 70-80% of available RAM, leaving headroom for the OS and other MySQL memory needs
Exactly 100% of available RAM
No more than 5% of available RAM
A fixed 512 MB regardless of server size
questions.explain: The lesson cites roughly 70-80% of RAM as a starting guideline, leaving room for the OS and other overhead, with the exact number needing real measurement.

questions.q: What tradeoff does innodb_log_file_size control, per this lesson?
options: Flush frequency for write-heavy workloads versus how long crash recovery takes
How many indexes a table can have
Whether mysqldump can be used at all
The number of secondary indexes InnoDB allows
questions.explain: A smaller log file forces more frequent dirty-page flushing; a larger one increases crash-recovery time since more log must be replayed.

questions.q: Why does this lesson caution against setting max_connections too high on a memory-constrained server?
options: Each connection carries memory overhead, so too many can itself cause the memory pressure that hurts performance
MySQL refuses to start if max_connections exceeds 100
max_connections has no relationship to memory usage
Higher max_connections always improves query speed regardless of memory
questions.explain: Connection buffers and sort buffers consume memory per connection, so an overly high max_connections can create memory pressure.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend using to right-size max_connections with real data?
options: Comparing the configured max_connections against the actual Max_used_connections observed in practice
Always setting it to the theoretical maximum MySQL allows
Copying the value from an unrelated server's configuration
Disabling connection limits entirely
questions.explain: Comparing SHOW VARIABLES for max_connections against SHOW STATUS for Max_used_connections grounds the setting in observed real usage.
